papers.title_in_file: A Preprocessing Perspective for Quantum Machine Learning Classification Advantage Using NISQ Algorithms
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, datasets, simulators, results and discussion read; appendix tables skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of dimensionality reduction (PCA, LDA, SVD, SKPP) before quantum encoding for a quantum SVM and a variational classifier on two finance datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that using Linear Discriminant Analysis in preprocessing gave a gain in balanced accuracy for the variational quantum algorithm, which outperformed baseline classical classifiers.
quotes: This study shows that we can achieve better classical encoding and performance of quantum classifiers by using Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) during the data preprocessing step.
Variational Quantum Algorithm (VQA) shows a gain of performance in balanced accuracy with the LDA technique and outperforms baseline classical classifiers.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on two datasets, with a 2-qubit simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: The word outperforms is the authors' own; the discussion says classical methods with dimensionality reduction are comparable, so the margin over a reduced classical baseline is not established here.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum models were run on a subsample of 800 training and 200 test samples with two qubits, on simulators only, with noise removed.
quotes: The subsample is constituted of 800 samples for the training phase and 200 for the test phase.
This choice is motivated by focusing on only two qubits to compare the results.
In our case, we subtracted the noise from the simulations.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that dimensionality reduction also improves the classical methods, that the quantum algorithms are comparable to them, and that more work is needed to fully demonstrate the advantages.
quotes: The DR also improves the performances of these methods, but quantum algorithms are comparable
but more work is needed to fully demonstrate the advantages.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its limits.

assertions.value: The authors state that the classical models used default parameters and were not tuned on the two datasets, and that only two datasets were used.
quotes: Classical ML methods selected for this study weren't tuned specifically on the two datasets. Default parameters were
Also, in this study, we used only two datasets close to the real-world data in the finance domain.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its limits.

assertions.value: The authors report a classical algorithm that, for a circuit on N qubits and a single Pauli observable, computes the coefficients of all trigonometric monomials up to a degree m in a time bounded by O(N 2m).

papers.title_in_file: No Free Lunch for Quantum Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, preliminaries, statement of the quantum NFL theorem, the QNN case study and conclusions read; the supplementary proof was skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper generalizing the classical No Free Lunch theorem to a lower bound on the quantum risk of learning an unknown unitary from input-output state pairs.

assertions.value: The paper derives a lower bound on the quantum risk, the probability that a trained hypothesis is incorrect on a random input, for a quantum learning algorithm trained on pairs of input and output states, averaged over training pairs and unitaries.
quotes: We find a lower bound on the quantum risk (the probability that a trained hypothesis is incorrect when presented with a random input) of a quantum learning algorithm trained via pairs of input and output states when averaged over training pairs and unitaries.
assertions.certainty_reason: A theorem derived in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum NFL gives an apparently stronger lower bound than its classical counterpart.
quotes: The quantum NFL provides an apparently stronger lower bound than its classical counterpart.
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement about the paper's own derived bound.

assertions.value: The authors state that the training pairs are assumed ideal and realisable, and that the hypothesis must reproduce the unknown unitary exactly on the training inputs.

papers.title_in_file: Microwave signal processing using an analog quantum reservoir computer
papers.version_note: The file is arXiv 2312.16166v2 dated 6 Sep 2024 (folder and file name carry 2023); title matches the record.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results text for the three tasks, and discussion read; methods and appendices skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: An experiment using a superconducting oscillator coupled to a qubit as an analog quantum reservoir to classify microwave signals.

assertions.value: The authors report that the reservoir classified which of 10 digital modulation classes a signal belongs to with more than 90% accuracy using 8 qubit-oscillator measurements in less than a millisecond, while a linear classifier reached 20%.
quotes: We note that in less than a millisecond, or with less than 2000 symbols, the reservoir was able to classify which of the 10 classes a given signal belongs to with > 90% accuracy when using 8 qubit-oscillator measurements.
A linear classifier can only achieve 20% classification accuracy for this task, even with infinite symbols.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one hardware experiment.

assertions.value: The authors report 93% accuracy in classifying six different sources of noise in only 2000 shots.
quotes: On the task of classifying over six different sources of noise, we achieved 93% accuracy (Fig. 4c) in only 2000 shots.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one hardware experiment.
